CEO transition announced Jan 17, 2025 (Killoy retires May 2025, Seyfert effective Mar 1, 2025); small-cap re-rating likely drove the index removal.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 largest customers: Lipsey's 28%, Sports South 18%, Davidson's 16%. FY23: Lipsey's 24%, Davidson's 19%, Sports South 15%. FY22: Lipsey's 23%, Davidson's 23%, Sports South 21%.
rfm_tuples.f: Customer concentration trajectory: top-3 share = 62% (2024) vs 58% (2023) vs 67% (2022). Lipsey's specifically grew 23 -> 24 -> 28 over three years -- material creep with largest distributor. Mode-B: derive whether share gain is genuine end-demand (sell-through > shipments) or channel-stuffing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top-3 = 62% (+4pp YoY). Lipsey's crossed the 25% concentration threshold (28% vs 24% YoY). Davidson's declined (19% -> 16%); Sports South grew (15% -> 18%). Critically: 4pp share gain at Lipsey's coincided with FY24 distributor inventory drawdown (-63.5k units) -- so this is genuine sell-through share gain, NOT channel-stuffing. RGR disclosed all three top customers by name (transparent).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is candid but concentration trend is a forward risk. Single distributor at 28% means Lipsey's financing health or strategic pivot can materially move RGR. Filing explicitly warns loss of any distributor 'may have a material adverse effect on the Company's financial results for a particular period.' Risk is real but not obscured.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 company finished-goods inventory decreased 28,300 units; distributor inventories decreased 63,500 units. Total channel: 311.0k (2024) vs 402.8k (2023) vs 411.2k (2022) -- channel inventory down 23% YoY.
rfm_tuples.f: Inventory build into a demand trough is the canonical firearms-industry distress tell. Mode-B unit reconciliation: production - shipments must equal finished-goods delta; shipments - sell-through must equal distributor inventory delta.
rfm_tuples.M_value: RECONCILED: Production 1,379.5k - Shipments 1,407.8k = -28.3k (matches stated). Distributor shipments-in 1,407.8k - sell-through 1,471.3k = -63.5k (matches stated). Channel destocking is REAL: producing BELOW shipments and shipments BELOW retail sell-through. OPPOSITE of the firearms-distress pattern. Adjusted NICS -4% but RGR sell-through +5% = market-share gain. Q1 2025 caveat: company finished goods inverted to +15,300 units build.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: RGR managed FY24 production conservatively; channel inventory drawn down to support distributor margins (vs competitors using aggressive promotions, discounts, rebates per RGR MD&A). Mode-B fully verifies. Q1 2025 reversal is a yellow flag for the next 2-3 quarters but not yet a distress signal.

Production +18% YoY while sell-through -8% YoY is a 26-point divergence -- the very pattern that historically presages firearms-industry inventory writedowns.

RGR is using Q1 2025 over-production to absorb fixed costs and post +9.7% NI optic while channel demand decelerates. NOT lying (fully disclosed), but IS the early-warning pattern for a firearms-cycle inventory writedown in 2-3 quarters if sell-through doesn't recover.

summary: RGR is the canonical honesty-alpha PASS case in the delisted_or_distressed group. The forensic framework finds essentially no lying or obscuring: zero long-term debt, $105M liquidity, undrawn revolver, current ratio 4.2x, orderly pre-announced CEO succession (Killoy -> Seyfert) with continuous CFO/auditor (RSM since 2005), formulaic 40%-of-NI dividend policy operating exactly per disclosure, counter-cyclical buyback into the trough funded with cash and no leverage, channel destocking of 23% in FY24 to support distributor margins (the OPPOSITE of the firearms-industry distress pattern), and NICS data fully verifiable against public NSSF series. The 9pp market-share gain in FY24 (sell-through +5% vs NICS -4%) is real and product-driven (Ruger American Gen II, Marlin lever-action revival, RXM). Two genuine concerns surface only via Mode-B claim evolution against the Q1 2025 10-Q: (i) top distributor Lipsey's concentration creep from 24% -> 28% YoY, and (ii) Q1 2025 production +18% YoY while sell-through -8% YoY, building company finished goods +15.3k units -- a borrow-earnings-from-the-future pattern that historically precedes Q3/Q4 production cuts in this cyclical industry. Neither is severe; both are fully disclosed. NET: RGR's drawdown and small-cap-index removal are SECTOR-CYCLICAL artifacts (NICS down 7% from 2021 peak), not company-specific disclosure failures. Under honesty-alpha framework, RGR is a LONG-tier candidate -- the 're-detecting honestly disclosed cyclical pain isn't alpha' principle from the small-cap pilot applies. The framework's contribution here is correct EXCLUSION-style: there is nothing to flag, and the absence of red flags is itself the signal.
